title: What Is Artificial Intelligence?
introduction: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the idea that machines can do tasks that usually need human thinking. Understanding AI helps us see how technology works in our daily lives.

sections.heading: Defining Artificial Intelligence
paragraphs: AI means a computer or device can perform tasks that normally need human thought, like recognizing pictures or understanding speech.
It tries to act like a brain by learning from data and making decisions.

example.title: AI Definition Example
example.content: When a phone suggests the next word while you type, it is using AI to predict your intention.

sections.heading: Why It Is Called Intelligence
paragraphs: The word "intelligence" is used because the system can solve problems, learn, and adapt, similar to how people do.
It does not think like a human, but it can handle tasks that need reasoning.

example.title: Smart Assistant
example.content: Siri understands spoken questions and gives answers, showing a form of machine intelligence.

sections.heading: AI vs. Traditional Software
sections.subheading: Key differences in how they work
paragraphs: Traditional software follows fixed rules written by programmers. AI systems learn patterns from data and improve over time.
Because AI learns, it can handle new situations that were not explicitly programmed.

example.title: Rule‑Based vs. Learning
example.content: A calculator follows exact formulas, while an AI program can improve its answers by learning from past calculations.

sections.heading: Everyday AI Examples
sections.subheading: Common AI you see every day
paragraphs: Many apps use AI to recommend movies, music, or products based on your past choices.
Navigation apps predict traffic and suggest faster routes using AI analysis.

example.title: Shopping Recommendations
example.content: Online stores show products you might like based on your browsing history, using AI to analyze patterns.

practice.title: Identify AI Around You
practice.instruction: Look around your home or phone and write down three things that use AI, such as voice assistants, photo tagging, or navigation suggestions.

keyTakeaways: AI means machines can perform tasks that normally need human intelligence.
AI learns from data, unlike traditional software that follows fixed rules.
Simple AI tools like voice assistants and recommendation systems are part of everyday life.

mcqs.question: What is the main difference between AI systems and traditional software?
options: AI follows fixed rules written by programmers
AI learns patterns from data and improves over time
mcqs.explanation: AI systems learn from data and can adapt, while traditional software follows static, programmer‑written rules.

mcqs.question: Which feature on a phone uses AI to predict the next word while you type?
mcqs.explanation: Predictive text analyzes your typing habits and uses AI to guess the word you intend to type next.

mcqs.question: Why is the word "intelligence" used to describe AI systems?
options: Because they can solve problems, learn, and adapt
Because they run faster than humans
Because they store large amounts of data
mcqs.explanation: AI is called intelligence because it can reason, learn from experience, and adjust its behavior, similar to human thinking.

mcqs.question: Which everyday application uses AI to suggest faster routes based on traffic conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Navigation apps analyze real‑time traffic data with AI algorithms to recommend quicker routes.

mcqs.question: According to the lesson, what is a key takeaway about AI compared to traditional software?
options: AI learns from data while traditional software follows fixed rules
Traditional software can adapt without new code
AI is only used in scientific labs
mcqs.explanation: A central point is that AI learns from data, unlike traditional software that relies on pre‑written, unchanging rules.
